In brief: The week ahead will be marked by a persistent low-pressure system that will bring widespread rainfall to Abuja, with temperatures ranging from 22°C to 29°C and humidity levels consistently above 90%. ### Monday The low-pressure system currently situated over the city will continue to dominate the weather pattern, leading to a high chance of rainfall throughout the day. Temperatures will rise to a high of 28°C, but the feels-like temperature will be closer to 30°C due to the high humidity levels, which will hover around 98%. This will make the air feel thick and muggy, particularly in low-lying areas such as Gwarinpa and the airport road. The rain is expected to start in the late morning, around 10 am, and will continue on and off throughout the day, with the heaviest downpours occurring in the late afternoon.
The wind will be relatively light, blowing at a speed of 7 km/h, which will do little to alleviate the humid conditions. As a result, residents can expect a rather uncomfortable day, with the heat index making the temperature feel several degrees higher than the actual reading. In areas such as Maitama and Wuse, the temperature will feel particularly oppressive due to the urban heat island effect, which will trap heat and moisture in the city. The rainfall accumulation is expected to range from 20 to 30 mm, with some areas potentially seeing even higher amounts. My best guess is that the rain will clear up by the evening, around 7 pm, but the skies will remain cloudy, keeping temperatures relatively warm overnight. The low temperature will dip to 22°C, but the humidity will remain high, making it feel more like 25°C. This will lead to a rather uncomfortable night, with the air feeling heavy and muggy. Residents can expect a similar pattern to emerge on Tuesday, with the low-pressure system still dominating the weather. For now, it appears that Monday will be the start of a rather wet and humid week, with residents advised to take necessary precautions to stay cool and dry.
